grades.quote: Instructions executing in machine mode have full privilege; a CPU starts in machine mode. Machine mode is mostly intended for setting up the computer during boot.
grades.reason: The passage directly explains the RISC-V M, S and U modes. Machine mode has full privilege and is used for boot setup. Supervisor mode runs the kernel and can execute privileged instructions. User mode runs applications and can execute only unprivileged instructions. It also covers how ecall moves from user to supervisor mode.
